summary: FBRX 2.3.1 Beta (Weft): the AI Toolkit, ready-made actions your AI runs and you can change, Fabrix troubleshooting your network through FBRX Server, and themes and governance in every edition.
notes: AI Toolkit (every edition): ready-made actions the AI runs in one step, such as your IP address, network adapters, DNS, a fixed or automatic address, the internet check and disk space. When it works out a new one it offers to keep it, and you can change any action's command; a change that could cut you off puts itself back unless you keep it.

Troubleshoot the network: let Fabrix look at your FBRX Server (FBRX Server → Let Fabrix look) and it checks FBRX Gate and MiniDome along with this computer. The server gives read-only access, and your password is not kept.
Every edition: Governance and the themes. A new computer asks whether you want the simple or the full menu, and which look.

Chats: send more while the AI works and they wait in a queue. The browser opens links in a new tab from the right-click menu, Ctrl+C stops the running command in Terminal, and notes open in a window of their own.
Editions: Standard includes 2 computers, Ultra 3 and Black Hole 5. An organization's members get their edition from FBRX Command, and support can be started from there in one step.
Ubuntu: uninstalling FBRX OS is one step (from its entry in your apps, or Settings), and Update now runs the installer for you.

server.summary: FBRX Server 1.4.1: the server's own terminal in the console, What if? before a gate change, and read-only access for Fabrix to troubleshoot your network.
notes: Server → Terminal: the server's shell in the browser for administrators, with Ctrl+C, Paste and full screen. Every session is in Users & audit and recorded on the server for 30 days.

FBRX Gate → Changes → What if?: before you commit, see who would gain or lose what, whether you would still reach the console, and which of the last hour's real connections the change would cut off. The server's AI can explain it.
Fabrix on your computer can look at the gate and MiniDome to troubleshoot the network, with read-only access you give it; Users & audit → Apps with access shows and revokes it.
From 1.1: sudo fbrx-server update check, then sudo fbrx-server update commit.

digger.summary: FBRX Digger 1.1.1: smaller and simpler, with device consoles in the Network Center and clearer sign-in errors.
notes: Links open in your own browser; Digger has no browser or edition settings of its own.
Device consoles (SSH, Telnet) are a tab of the Network Center; a sign-in that fails says why, and trying again keeps the device's key; a successful SSH sign-in opens its session.
Digger has its own tray icon and menu.
